page.text: There is no formal enforcement body. Order is maintained through community social pressure, the authority of established families, and the implicit threat of collective action against those who break the peace. This works until it doesn't.
The town knows perfectly well what it could not survive, and the knowledge shapes what it will and will not provoke.
The site gives Schwarzwalde nothing defensively. Every advantage the town holds is one it has paid for and must keep paying for.
The town's usual posture has been set aside at Schwarzwalde. Everything is arranged for the one thing now, and the rest is waiting.
The crisis at Schwarzwalde has changed the posture and not the prospects, and the town has been careful to keep the two separate.

faces: The stallholders report the grain in the store as the one thing here worth coming for. What the town has put over it is a lock.
A travelling trader says he is asked to step round the thing leaning behind every door he calls at.
The older households have it that they have been asked for a bed for a stranger and a hand at a neighbour's roof. They have never been asked for a wall.
Those who sit to hear a matter hold that nothing a wall would have kept out has ever come before them.
Whoever buries the dead says opening the ground has never been anybody's wage here, the people nearest doing it between them.
At the tavern a carter says the nights are all the town pays to keep itself. Everything else gets done when work is over.
The trades pay into the purse like everybody else, a guild member says. The shutters on a workshop go up at the workshop's own charge.
A clerk in the hall has it that the purse that would have kept a wall up keeps the nights.
One of the watch says the wage he draws is the whole of what the town pays against an army.
unit.rendered: A travelling trader says he is asked to step round the thing leaning behind every door he calls at.
unit.spine: {settlement} has no line around it and no soldiers of its own. What keeping there is falls to the people who live here, out of their own hours.

faces: A stranger wronged here asks where to take it, a travelling trader says, and is pointed at the door of the house that did it.
At the tavern they say a stranger owed money here should take it in goods and not wait on coin.
The elders say they hear a stranger's wrong as they hear anyone's, and a stranger who does not stay for the answer was not much wronged.
Whoever digs the ground holds that it takes a stranger on the same terms as anyone, whatever was or was not agreed about him.
At the gate they say a stranger is looked over on the way in, and nothing is kept of the looking.
The muster tells a stranger who complains that there is nowhere to lock up the man he names. There is nowhere for the stranger either.
The stallholders say a stranger cheated here has no board to go to, and would do better to come back to the stall.
unit.rendered: The elders say they hear a stranger's wrong as they hear anyone's, and a stranger who does not stay for the answer was not much wronged.
unit.spine: A traveller wronged here finds there is nowhere to take it, and nobody local expected there to be.

faces: The bar at the way through is kept by the doors nearest it, those who hold the way say. Whoever lifts it leaves it to the next of those doors.
Those who keep the ground hold that nobody is turned away from the digging, and whoever owns the spade brings the spade.
The pails at the water each carry a household's own mark, a stranger says, and a visitor is handed the unmarked pail.
The muster says the bows and the spears it would carry are the ones it hunts with. Nobody ever promised it a better spear.
The elders say the turn comes round to everyone who can spare a back.
At the tavern they say the turn comes round to the same backs and never as far as the next roof.
The store the soldiers eat out of is the store the place eats out of, by their own account. No one has walked them past its shelves.
One of the watch says the round is walked before anything is settled. The purse comes after the roof, the water and the grain.
The ask falls on whoever sets out a stall, the stallholders say, and everybody else comes in with a basket.
Those who hear disputes say the quarrel that reaches them is over who owed a turn, and the turn itself was taken by a neighbour.
unit.rendered: The elders say the turn comes round to everyone who can spare a back.
unit.spine: The means here come short of what trouble takes. The households make up the difference.

faces: The older households say a sick house here is never left to itself.
At the tavern they say the houses that are sat up with are the houses that sit up with others.
The food left on a step is how a sick house is known from the lane, a traveller reports.
At the market they say a house with somebody ill in it comes for vinegar and roots, and whoever has them names the price.
Those who bury the dead reckon they are the one trade here that is sent for in a bad year and not thanked for coming.

Schwarzwalde was held a generation on and the arrangements made then are the arrangements the town still runs on.

page.label: historicalCharacter
page.text: The Flood did not destroy the settlement. It destroyed the settlement's sense of itself. What came after was rebuilt from the ground up, including what people believed about where they lived
The fields begin where Schwarzwalde loses interest, and not before.
Nothing in Schwarzwalde is arranged for buying and selling in quantity, which tells a stranger the essential thing about the place.
Schwarzwalde keeps few institutions because it needs few; what a larger town does with buildings, this one does with acquaintance.

page.label: crisis.label
page.text: Infiltrated

page.label: crisis.summary
page.text: Schwarzwalde has been quietly penetrated by an outside interest. Enemy agents, a cult, a merchant intelligence network. The settlement does not know. Key decisions are being subtly shaped.

page.label: crisis.hook
page.text: Something is slightly wrong: a decision that doesn't make sense, a face seen in too many places, a piece of information that reached the wrong hands. The players can notice if they pay attention.
There is no visible crisis. The pattern is legible only to whoever is counting the coincidences.
There is no crisis on the books. Whatever strain the settlement carries, it carries at a weight it can hold.
The strain is severe. Schwarzwalde is meeting it by giving up things it would rather keep.
The condition is deepening. The town's response has not caught up with the rate.

Schwarzwalde is neither rich nor poor, and the fact that nothing about it is remarkable is the most accurate thing to say about it.
Schwarzwalde expects to go on being Schwarzwalde.
Schwarzwalde's defences are a gesture, and it is not a gesture anyone is fooled by.
Schwarzwalde keeps no muster worth the name; the gate is shut at night by whoever is nearest to it.
Schwarzwalde has no answer to what lives beyond its fields and nobody whose work it would be.
Little is reported at Schwarzwalde, because reporting produces no outcome.
Schwarzwalde runs close to what it takes in: one interruption would reach the households inside the season.
Schwarzwalde keeps no practitioner, no arrangement, and no expectation of either.
Schwarzwalde's security is its own harvest, which means it is proof against a closed road and not against a bad year.

page.label: arrivalScene
page.text: Schwarzwalde looks exactly like it should. The gate is attended, the market sounds busy, there is nothing remarkable about the approach. Everything is as it should be. The settlement is small enough that you can see all of it from the road: half-timbered upper floors project above the busier lanes. A magelight lamp post marks the main gate. Schwarzwalde is announced by the smoke of its cookfires and the sound of its market before its buildings are visible.

page.label: pressureSentence
page.text: Three separate things have gone slightly wrong in Schwarzwalde recently, in ways that look like bad luck; they are not bad luck.
Schwarzwalde is a road town that has outgrown its fields, and it is buying the difference.
Schwarzwalde is a handful of roofs with a reason, and the reason is usually the ground.
Of everything Schwarzwalde is tied into, one connection comes up first whenever the town explains itself.
The people of Schwarzwalde are connected the way the people of any settled place are connected, and there is no more to say about it than that.

page.label: prominentRelationship
page.text: Vilbirg Becker's relationship with Liutgar Bauer is more complicated than their public roles suggest. The balance of leverage has recently shifted. One party has noticed; the other hasn't yet.

page.text: institutions: Informal elder consensus, Burial ground, Dwellings (4-16), Water source, Access to external mill, Subsistence farming, Shepherd collective

page.label: chain.absence
page.text: No named seat-holder stands in the record. The chain ends, honestly, at the faction.
The Elder Council holds Schwarzwalde on sufferance: nothing it asks is refused outright and nothing it asks arrives quickly, which is its own kind of answer.
Schwarzwalde keeps one plain accusation against the Elder Council (that it has left the town open) and brings it out again whenever anything else goes wrong.

page.label: powerStructure.stability
page.text: Stable

page.label: governingName
page.text: Elder Council

page.label: recentConflict
page.text: A dispute over grazing rights and water access has been running for two seasons. It has stopped being about grazing rights and water access.
A stranger doing business at Schwarzwalde needs one name and gets one answer, and can plan a season ahead on the strength of it.

page.pool: governing faction holds a DOMINANT share
page.text: No rival at Schwarzwalde moves against Elder Council, and it is not restraint. The arithmetic of the thing is plain to everybody who has done it.
The hall at Schwarzwalde is not organized into sides. The factions sit as factions, and nothing binds any two of them into anything larger.
The town's business goes to a body rather than a person, and everybody has learned how long a body takes.

page.text: A stranger who addresses the Elder Council at Schwarzwalde by any other title is corrected, politely and immediately.
